title: Bram and the Hollow
premise: Mara Lockridge, a memory-thief who trades in other people's pasts to escape her own, is cornered by a dying courier who presses a map of the Hollow into her hands and begs her to finish his contract: steal back the soul of a child sold to the court beneath Thornfell mountain. Hunted by the smugglers' guild she betrayed and shadowed by Bram, an amnesiac boy whose missing memories are the map's missing key, Mara descends into the Hollow where debts are paid in years and justice belongs to whoever holds the ledger. To free the child's soul, Mara must sacrifice the one memory she has never sold — her sister's face — but at the final turn of the moon she discovers the court will accept a substitute: the courier's own soul, still bound in Bram's body. She frees both children by forging the ledger itself, condemning the Hollow's magistrates to forget their own names, and walks out of the mountain with a found family instead of a fortune.
about_author: Oscar Kavanagh is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing smugglers' ledgers in border-town libraries before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people the law forgot, from a house built on an old toll road.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. In the smuggling town of Grayhollow, Mara extracts a merchant's first love from his mind and sells it to a grieving widow, establishing her trade and her rule: never keep what you steal. When she refuses a job from the Vane family guild, they mark her for collection. Emotional beat: loneliness worn as armor.

chapters.title: A Stranger on the Toll Road
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A bleeding courier collapses at her door with a map tattooed in shifting ink on his skin and a child's soul-token around his neck. He presses both into her hands as guild hunters close in, whispering 'thirteen turns' before dying. Emotional beat: reluctant inheritance — she never agreed to this.

chapters.title: What the Ink Remembers
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The map won't show its paths to her; it flickers and hides. Studying the courier's effects, she finds a sketch of a boy labeled 'Bram' and realizes the map responds to memories it recognizes. Emotional beat: frustration curdling into obsession as the guild burns her safehouse.

chapters.title: The Boy Without a Yesterday
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Introduced hiding in Grayhollow's undercrofts, Bram remembers nothing but how to survive and a lullaby he cannot place. Guild hunters nearly take him; Mara intercepts, recognizing the map's ink glowing on his wrist. Emotional beat: two broken people circling each other with mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: Terms of an Unwilling Contract
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara interrogates Bram; touching his mind, she glimpses the Hollow's court and a cell of caged lights — souls. The map completes itself when she holds his hand: thirteen moon-turns remain, and three are already gone. Emotional beat: dread becoming resolve; she stops planning her escape.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Road South
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They flee through Thornfell's passes using Mara's knowledge and Bram's eerie instinct for hidden ways. A guild ambush forces them to trust each other completely for the first time. Emotional beat: the first fragile stitch of found family, sewn under arrow-fire.

chapters.title: The Widow of Candlemere
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. In a mountain village they seek the courier's contact, an old woman who bought her own daughter's memory back from Mara years ago. She reveals the Hollow's law: souls are collateral, and the court honors only forged or stolen claims. Emotional beat: shame — Mara meets a debt she created.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns, Ten Remaining
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram dreams in fragments: a courtroom of antlered magistrates, a smaller hand in his. He begins to suspect the stolen soul is someone he loved. Mara deflects, but the lullaby he hums matches one she knows. Emotional beat: grief arriving before understanding.

chapters.title: The Gate That Eats Names
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. They reach the Hollow's mouth, a cave that strips travelers of their names unless paid in memory. Mara pays with a stranger's memory from her stock; Bram, having nothing, passes through untouched — the gate already considers him empty. Emotional beat: horror at what the mountain values.

chapters.title: Market of the Unpaid Dead
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Inside the Hollow: a bazaar where ghosts sell regrets and years. They barter for passage and learn the soul-token belongs to Wren, the courier's daughter, held until the thirteenth turn when her debt converts to servitude forever. Emotional beat: urgency sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Ledger Below
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Guided by a disgraced clerk-ghost named Ivo, they infiltrate the Hall of Accounts, where every debt in the mountain is written. Mara discovers the Vane guild holds shares in Wren's bond — her old enemies profit from this. Emotional beat: rage reframed as strategy; justice needs a plan, not fury.

chapters.title: Antlered Magistrates
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Summoned unwillingly before the court, Bram stands before the magistrates and they address him by a name he doesn't know: the courier's brother, memory-wiped as payment for his own old debt. Emotional beat: identity shattering — he is evidence, not a person, to them.

chapters.title: The Memory She Never Sold
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The court offers Mara a bargain: Wren's freedom for her most guarded memory — her sister's face, the last thing she owns. Alone, she weighs it against the growing truth that Bram and Wren are her responsibility now. Emotional beat: the thief asked, finally, to give rather than take.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Turn of the Moon
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo, desperate to buy back his own name, sells their plan to the magistrates. Bram is seized; Mara escapes with the token but not the boy. Emotional beat: betrayal's bitter taste — and Mara realizing she cannot finish this alone, which terrifies her more than the court.

chapters.title: Debts Among Thieves
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara calls in every favor in the Hollow's market, rallying the unpaid dead and cheated vendors she's befriended. The widow of Candlemere arrives with villagers; even the guild's low-level smugglers defect when shown the Vanes' ledger shares. Emotional beat: found family made literal — an army of the overlooked.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Turn
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. In a court cell, Bram recovers a fragment: he volunteered his memory to hide Wren's soul inside himself — the token is a decoy; the true bond lives in his mind. Emotional beat: self-sacrifice remembered too late, courage recovered from ruin.

chapters.title: Storming the Hall of Accounts
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. On the twelfth turn's eve, Mara's ragged alliance assaults the Hall while she slips in through routes only a memory-thief could find. She reaches the master ledger and finds the court's founding crime: the magistrates bought their immortality with a whole village's souls. Emotional beat: righteous clarity — the law below is theft wearing robes.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Confronted by the magistrates, Mara does what she does best: she steals. Entry by entry, she lifts the magistrates' memories of their own names and crimes, forging the ledger so the court's power unravels. Emotional beat: triumph with teeth — justice delivered by the criminal they scorned.

chapters.title: The Price of the Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The collapsing court demands a final payment to release Wren's soul. Bram offers himself, but Mara intervenes, paying her sister's memory after all — freely given, which the old law must honor. Emotional beat: grief and grace entwined; the cost is real and permanent.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Wren wakes in Bram's arms; the siblings' shattered memories begin returning in pieces, incomplete but shared. The freed souls of the old village rise through the mountain like embers going home. Emotional beat: reunion without wholeness — healing as a beginning, not a fix.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Let Go
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The Hollow seals behind them. Mara grieves her sister's face, unable to recall it, until Wren — who met her once in the court's halls — describes her, giving the memory back secondhand. Emotional beat: sorrow transmuted; some things can be returned by others.

chapters.title: The House on the Toll Road
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, epilogue tone. Months later, Mara runs a new trade from Candlemere: recovering stolen memories for the exploited, with Bram, Wren, and Ivo (name newly re-earned) beside her. The guild is broken; the map's ink fades, its work done. Emotional beat: quiet arrival — a thief who finally keeps something worth keeping.
